title: Peach Bounce 0.1 — Gravity Sling
prompt:
DIRECT PLAYER DESIGN BRIEF — IMPLEMENT, NOT JUST DISCUSS. Transform the existing Peach Bounce game at its SAME stable URL into a new, self-contained, lightweight mobile HTML5 game called "Peach Bounce 0.1 · Gravity Sling". The old paddle/tray, bouncing peach and 15 jam tiles are OBSOLETE; replace the core gameplay, art, instructions, scoring, and end state. The existing host contracts (Play/Pause/Restart, real touch, keyboard, responsive Canvas, read-only BORHEZ_GAME snapshot, accessibility and publication) remain.

THE GAME: A 2D space/fruit arcade seen in tilted 2.5D perspective: a converging runway/depth grid toward a horizon near the top, with oncoming fruit starting small in the distance and visibly growing as they approach the ship at the bottom. Depth changes apparent size and position; gameplay remains Canvas 2D, no heavy 3D engine.

CONTROLS: The ONLY gameplay input is sliding the gravity ship LEFT and RIGHT with one finger or left/right/A/D keyboard. No tap-to-fire, aiming joystick, up/down ship movement, keyboard-only mechanics or extra buttons during play. Probe launch, recapture and relaunch happen autonomously through gravity physics and ship positioning.

PROBE PHYSICS: The ship owns a finite reserve of visible probes and exerts a gravity-like attraction field on an active probe; each simulation step updates its actual position and velocity. The active probe travels upfield to collect/destroy fruit on contact, then gravity draws it back toward the moving ship. A visible annular CATCH / SLING ZONE around the ship recaptures the returning probe and automatically slings it outward/upfield; a closer return to the ship's center creates a FASTER launch than a grazing return. Ship movement alters the gravitational center and therefore trajectory, so lateral skill matters. Use bounded acceleration/velocity and deterministic fixed-step integration to avoid chaotic jumps, teleporting, permanent stalls or impossible early losses. Show an animated tether/field effect if useful, without adding another control.

DAMAGE AND LOSSES: Fruit colliding DIRECTLY with the ship (not intercepted by the probe) causes exactly one hull damage event with brief invulnerability, destroys the current probe and reduces the ship's visible HULL count. If the active probe escapes too far/fully leaves the permitted arena, it is irretrievably lost and the visible PROBES reserve decreases. A replacement probe must automatically deploy (without a fire control) when available. If hull or probe supply is exhausted, end the round clearly and offer replay. Make normal play winnable: avoid immediately losing all probes due to uncontrollable starting velocities.

FRUIT WAVES: Incoming fruit arrive in distinct groups/waves with breaks. They move closer and grow as depth decreases but their *forward approach speed progressively slows near the ship*, giving time to intercept. Each group has a clear ORDERED destruction sequence, indicated legibly using numbered or colored fruit and a 'NEXT' indicator. Only the correct next fruit counts as cleared; wrong-order impacts cannot let the player bypass the order (give feedback and retain the target). Order determines the effective quickest solution; targets must remain reachable and waves cannot become impossible solely because the ship is constrained to horizontal movement. A cleared group advances to the next wave, with gradual tactical variety and appropriately balanced challenge. Show WAVES, SCORE, HULL and PROBES.

AGENT DEVELOPMENT: Designer, Researcher, and Engineer each independently propose actual code-level subsystems OF THIS SAME CONCEPT: perspective/waves, gravity probe/catch physics, and ship/loss/input integration. Critic compares compatibility and Producer agrees at least two compatible proposals, but the coder must implement ALL the mandatory game mechanics above regardless of which proposed subsystems are selected. Do not replace the concept with other minigames. Record agreements and test evidence; only deploy if the whole playable gravity-sling game passes QA. Keep it instant-loading and usable on mobile portrait.
acceptance: The existing studio-original-001 game URL is retained and visible page title shows Peach Bounce 0.1 — Gravity Sling; old tray, 15 jam tiles and old timer/win logic are replaced by the new gameplay, not cosmetically reskinned.
Only left/right horizontal ship dragging and keyboard left/right/A/D move the player; no manual shooting or vertical player control, while play/pause/restart buttons work.
Draw a 2D tilted depth perspective with a distant horizon, receding lanes, and fruit sprites that visibly enlarge while approaching the ship; no external 3D or runtime dependencies.

An active probe has persistent physical position and velocity; ship-relative gravity curves the trajectory. The probe automatically flies upfield, intercepts fruit, and can return to the ship without teleporting.
A visible catch-zone captures returning probes and automatically relaunches them; central catches create measurably faster launches than edge catches, and ship x-movement changes the trajectory.
On direct fruit-to-ship collision, hull decreases once, the active probe is destroyed, damage cooldown prevents multiple immediate hull losses and the HUD reflects the consequences.
An escaped probe is permanently lost, visible probe count drops and another automatically deploys from finite stock. Hull or probe exhaustion ends the game; restart restores original counts.
Fruit arrive in spaced groups/waves, approaching from distance while progressively SLOWING their depth travel as they near the ship, giving controllable interception windows.
Every wave has an explicitly displayed NEXT ordered target. Correct next-target hits remove fruit and increase progress; wrong-order contacts do not remove later targets or reward skipping.
Wave completion advances progression with readable score/wave/HULL/PROBES status, clear win/lose or survival end condition, replay, and increasing but fair challenge.

The gameplay council records independent code-symbol proposals, Critic compatibility and Producer agreed integration; integrated source implements the full player specification rather than merely two selected optional subfeatures.

Independent 360x780 and 390x844 mobile touch/browser tests, JS syntax, pause/freeze, restart/reset, visual change and game-specific physics/loss/wave checks must pass before hash-verified production delivery.
